data.narrative:
Squint is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $59M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of three same-sector, same-stage private peers—Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B)—alongside one public comparable and eight additional private benchmarks across the sector.

Two triangulation methods are applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy for pre-money valuation, applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, implying $112M. Peer-median analysis across the three direct comparables yields $1.8B, with a range of $1.6B to $2.0B. The peer-median method reflects market valuations for robotics companies at identical development stage, though the width of that range ($400M spread) signals meaningful variance in how the market prices comparable risk and revenue profiles within this cohort.

The triangulated range spans $95M (conservative stage-progression floor) to $2.0B (peer-median ceiling), with a median of $931M across the two methods. This wide dispersion reflects structural uncertainty: the stage-progression method depends entirely on capital-as-proxy assumptions, while peer comparables remain sensitive to unmeasured differences in revenue run-rate, unit economics, and customer concentration. Resolution of valuation within this band would require visibility into Squint's revenue trajectory and competitive differentiation relative to the three named peers.
